Athena Online · Private run-through

The clinic, still with you between sessions.

Athena Online is a clinic and client web app that carries the clinical relationship beyond the treatment room, so that a client leaves their first session with a real programme on their phone, keeps progressing between visits, and has somewhere to stay once the pain has settled and the bigger goal is still ahead of them.

Designed and built by Dr David Silver PhD, Chartered Physiotherapist, Athena Physio, Cobham and The Forge Clinic, Richmond.

The problem

Private physiotherapy has a cliff at discharge.

Care stops when the pain does

  • Once symptoms settle the one-to-ones end, the structure around the client disappears, and the gains made in clinic quietly fade.
  • The goal that actually matters to the client, a half marathon, a return to sport, a busy life without flare-ups, is usually still months away.

Support leaks out for free

  • Between sessions, help travels by text, WhatsApp and favours, which is unpaid, unlimited and impossible to scale.
  • Previously, open messaging through a third-party programme app had become exactly this kind of unpaid support channel, costing significant clinician time.

The relationship has nowhere to live

  • The trust built in the room is the most valuable thing in the practice, yet there is no natural place for it to continue once treatment winds down.
  • A large client base built over many years has no simple way back in.
The idea

Value is given first, and commitment is only ever invited afterwards.

The commercial model falls out of good clinical practice. A concrete goal set in the first session turns treatment into a journey, and a journey is something a client wants someone alongside them for. David never sells; when the time is right, the platform makes the offer.

1

First session

A concrete goal is agreed, and the client leaves with their programme already on their phone, with David's videos and coaching cues.

"I walked out knowing exactly what to do."

2

The first gap

Sessions are followed day by day; missed sessions are flagged and check-ins come back to the clinic.

"It felt like he was still keeping an eye on me."

3

Follow-ups

David opens each appointment already knowing how the week went, and the programme progresses in four-week blocks.

"It changed as I got better."

4

The inflection

As in-person sessions space out, the app presents membership as continued care towards the client's own goal.

"I'm not being dropped."

5

Ongoing

New blocks, check-ins and fresh goals, with a paid one-to-one whenever something needs hands-on care.

"He's staying with me until I get there."

No card before value

The client's programme is theirs to keep either way, so the free experience feels complete rather than like a teaser.

The platform makes the offer

Every word David says stays clinical. Pricing and membership live in the app, at the point care naturally eases.

Goals renew the relationship

Pain relief is a destination; a goal is a journey, and each goal reached opens the next one.

The client app

What a client sees on their phone.

A branded, mobile-first web app that opens from a link, so there is nothing to download from an app store. Clients are set up by David and log in with their own account. Screens below are from the live build, shown with a test account.

The clinic workspace

Where David builds, assigns and keeps track.

The clinic side is organised around a reusable library, so that a programme is assembled from parts that already exist rather than written from scratch for every client.

The Vault

One home for every reusable piece of content: exercises, blocks, workouts, cardio workouts, programmes and cardio programmes, plus settings for equipment, programme phases, email templates and brand packs.

Each exercise carries a stable ID, a Vimeo video, a default prescription by reps and sets or time under load, coaching cues, body parts and equipment.

A branded exercise library

182 exercises with branded thumbnails, filterable by body part, equipment and role in a session (warm-up, activation, main body, injury prevention and cool-down). A "Needs video" filter shows exactly what still has to be filmed.

Blocks with built-in progression

Blocks are typed groups of exercises with their own week-to-week progression, usually over four weeks, and they are the building bricks of every workout.

  • Activations: reaction and readiness work that opens a session
  • Injury prevention blocks
  • A cardio library of reusable prescriptions, from easy swims to structured return-to-run steps

Cardio library

Walking, bike, swim and treadmill prescriptions that can be dropped into any workout, including walking progressions and a staged return-to-run sequence.

Messages that protect clinician time

Every conversation in one inbox, with anyone who has waited more than a day for a reply flagged. Clients without a messaging tier get one free message per programme; after that the app explains membership instead of the message reaching David, and the inbox counts those moments as membership prompts.

Running the business

Coach accounts with control over which programme templates each coach can see, a record of every purchase, a client sign-up QR code for the clinic, registrations, access windows and forms.

How programmes are made

Clinical judgement stays with the clinician, and the app does the carrying.

Every programme is David's clinical decision. Strength work is built by hand from the library, while running and other cardio plans are prepared with an AI assistant outside the app and then imported, so the app itself stays simple, reliable and free of automated clinical decisions.

In clinicAssessment and goal

The session note and an agreed goal set the direction.

StrengthBuilt from blocks

David assembles workouts from library blocks that progress over four weeks.

CardioPlanned, then imported

A per-client plan is prepared and pasted in as a plan code, filling the weekly calendar.

ClientOn their phone

Sessions, videos, a weekly calendar and a downloadable plan.

Logged sessions and check-ins flow back to the clinic, so each follow-up starts from what actually happened that week. In-app AI drafting has been built and deliberately switched off for launch, keeping every decision human-reviewed.

Revenue model

Four membership tiers, offered as continued care.

Subscriptions are sold on the web rather than through an app store, which avoids app store commission on every payment. One-to-one sessions in clinic continue alongside, as they do today.

TierPriceShape of the offer
Athena Member£5.99 / monthThe entry tier that keeps a client connected after rehab.
Athena Progress£24.99 / monthContinued progression towards the client's goal.
Athena Perform£49.99 / monthFor clients training towards a performance goal.
Athena Athlete Five places£149 / monthA weekly one-to-one with David, continuous reprogramming, and a direct line whenever something comes up.

Prices as currently shown in the app. The free single message per programme is the first place a client hears that ongoing support is available.

Built lean

A modern stack with very low running costs.

The app was built by David himself, directing an AI coding assistant step by step, on widely used, well-supported services. Costs stay close to nothing until clients are paying.

The stack

  • Next.js web app hosted on Vercel
  • Supabase for the database and secure logins
  • Stripe for subscriptions and payments
  • Vimeo for exercise video
  • Resend for client emails

Why it matters

  • No app store approval or commission
  • Works on any phone through a link
  • Brand packs let the same platform carry other Athena streams

Low fixed cost

  • Close to £0 while building
  • Card fees only once clients pay
  • Expensive extras such as wearable data are a later phase, funded by the top tier
£0Approximate monthly running cost during the build
£45 to £75Estimated monthly fixed cost once live with paying clients
4Athena Progress members would cover even the upper estimate

Running cost figures are planning estimates based on 2026 published service pricing, before card fees.
